cases.scenario: Create one person from a stable spawn event and resolve it after an ECS slot is recycled.
cases.oracle: PersonId remains unchanged and a recycled handle resolves only through its current generation.

cases.scenario: Close an episode and admit the same person again.
cases.oracle: Longitudinal identity is retained; the new episode is distinct and history remains queryable.

cases.scenario: Open overlapping episodes for one person in two services.
cases.oracle: Both episodes belong to one person; no duplicate person is created.

cases.scenario: Attach one episode to a second person after creation.
cases.oracle: Reject without changing either person's episode set or histories.

cases.scenario: Create another episode with an already-used EpisodeId.
cases.oracle: Reject without changing person, episode, accounting or RNG state.

cases.scenario: Resolve a stale ECS handle after its storage slot is reused for another entity.
cases.oracle: Stale handle cannot resolve to the replacement longitudinal identity.

cases.scenario: Add BirthParentOf(person, person).
cases.oracle: Reject atomically; no edge or accounting change.

cases.scenario: Add an edge that closes a path in BirthParentOf ancestry.
cases.oracle: Reject atomically; existing graph remains byte-equivalent.

cases.scenario: Create a cycle in an unrelated relation type whose contract permits cycles.
cases.oracle: BirthParentOf acyclicity does not become a global graph restriction.

cases.scenario: Replay a SpawnEventId with an identical canonical payload.
cases.oracle: No duplicate person, episode, edge, lifecycle event, or accounting count.

cases.scenario: Reuse a SpawnEventId with a different canonical payload.
cases.oracle: Reject atomically and preserve identity, lifecycle, accounting and RNG state.

cases.scenario: Use a different SpawnEventId to create an existing PersonId.
cases.oracle: Reject; a second event cannot take ownership of the identity.

cases.scenario: Remove a BirthParentOf edge while both persons and infant episodes exist.
cases.oracle: Only the edge is removed; persons, episodes, histories and other edges remain.

cases.scenario: Close the parent's episode while an infant has an active episode.
cases.oracle: Infant progression and episode continue independently.

cases.scenario: Apply service entry and exit for an existing person.
cases.oracle: Events affect service accounting, not longitudinal person creation/destruction.

cases.scenario: Record explicit death, then query prior links and episodes.
cases.oracle: Death is terminal to new activity while identity and history remain addressable.

cases.scenario: Create parent/infant links for an operative birth event.
cases.oracle: Delivery mode does not alter identity namespace or cardinality.

cases.scenario: One BirthEventId creates two infants, each with its own PersonId and stream namespace.
cases.oracle: One-to-many parent links; infants have independent identities and streams.

cases.scenario: Replay the same logical event history with 1, 2 and 4 workers and different traversal order.
cases.oracle: PersonIds, EpisodeIds, edge set and per-process draw streams are equivalent.

cases.scenario: Reject a conflicting spawn or relationship command between unrelated process events.
cases.oracle: Unrelated process random draws and event histories are unchanged.

cases.scenario: Checkpoint and restore with concurrent episodes, birth links, lifecycle state and replay keys.
cases.oracle: Identities, edges, terminal states and dedupe state round-trip exactly.

cases.scenario: Compare uninterrupted execution with checkpoint/restore followed by the same event suffix.
cases.oracle: Identity allocation, relationships, lifecycle counts and streams match.

cases.scenario: Retry a lifecycle event after a modeled compensation/recovery boundary.
cases.oracle: Stable event key prevents duplicate identity or accounting effect.

cases.scenario: Submit a fixed set of same-time identity commands, including two SpawnEventIds claiming one PersonId, in multiple arrival/traversal/worker orders.
cases.oracle: Canonical logical event order yields identical accepted/rejected event IDs, identity/relationship/lifecycle/accounting state and unrelated RNG streams for every permutation.

cases.scenario: Submit a new SpawnEventId whose logical time is already sealed by the identity ledger.
cases.oracle: Reject atomically; no identity, edge, lifecycle or accounting change; event ID remains unconsumed; RNG state is unchanged. Checkpoint replay, if separately requested, is a distinct operation.
